sections.overview: The Chinese Thrush is an endemic of China, breeding mainly in the country’s central mountains and moving to lower elevations outside the breeding season.
sections.identification: It has a pale eyebrow and white wing bars.
sections.habitat: It inhabits mountain broadleaf and mixed forests, especially damp woodland near streams with a rich shrub layer.
sections.diet: Its diet includes insects, especially caterpillars, as well as berries and other plant foods.
sections.behavior: It is shy and often stays singly or in pairs, foraging on the ground or in low shrubs.
sections.reproduction: The consulted regional accounts provide little detail on its breeding biology.
sections.ecology: At Tai Shan it is described as a passage migrant. Hong Kong records are scarce winter occurrences.
sections.conservation: The Hong Kong Bird Watching Society reports a stable population trend and Least Concern status.
